# Brāhmaṇadhammayāga Sutta (Iti 100 (It 4.1 PTS It 101))

**ID:** Iti 100 (It 4.1 PTS It 101)
**Section:** Itivuttaka (iti)
**Collection:** Sutta
**Title (Pali):** Brāhmaṇadhammayāga Sutta
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0504m.mul3.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Brāhmaṇadhammayāga Sutta* is the opening discourse of the fourth section of the *Itivuttaka* (Iti 100, It 4.1, PTS It 101). In this discourse, the Buddha depicts himself as a doctor and characterizes his monastic disciples as true heirs in the Dhamma rather than heirs in material things. In secondary scholarship, Richard S. Cohen notes that the sutta contains imagery of the Buddha's legitimate or "breast-born" (*aurasa*) son, presenting a parallel formulation to the *Aggañña Sutta* (DN 27), wherein the Buddha rejects Brahmanical claims of spiritual sovereignty from Brahmā's mouth by asserting that his disciples are born of the Dhamma [Cohen, Śākyabhikṣus].

Ireland [Cohen, Śākyabhikṣus].
